Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own.

We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific.

We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,700 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told…

sections.title: How you'll make impact
paras: Own the end-to-end delivery of complex client integrations that bring Airwallex’s global payments and financial products to life for enterprise partners, shopping carts, and payment gateways.

Translate agreed business requirements and solution designs into clear delivery plans, coordinating Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, Engineering, Operations, and external stakeholders to deliver on time, on scope, and to a high quality bar. You’ll manage work across scoping, solution design, onboarding, configuration, testing and certification, pilot, launch, and early optimisation, while keeping risks, dependencies, approvals, and trade-offs visible.

Lead partner projects alongside integration engineers, solution architects, technical account managers, and support teams. You’ll establish effective governance, operating rhythms, status reporting, and post-launch reviews, using delivery metrics such as time to go live, adherence to plan, and launch quality to improve our integration playbooks over time.

bullets: A bachelor’s degree in a related field.
5+ years of experience in product delivery management or project management, managing complex, multi-stakeholder technology or financial services implementations.
5+ years of professional services or client-facing delivery experience in a fast-paced environment, such as consulting, systems integration, or enterprise implementation.
Experience with global payment products or technology-led business solutions, with the ability to translate product capabilities into practical integration plans for partners.
A track record of successfully delivering cross-functional projects with stakeholders from diverse backgrounds and functions, including C-level executives, technical teams, and operations.
Exceptional written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to lead steering meetings, write clear status updates, and influence decisions without direct authority.

Hands-on experience working with or alongside integration engineers, solution architects, or technical program managers on API-based integrations, including familiarity with common web and API concepts.

sections.title: Preferred
bullets: Experience delivering large-scale partner integrations in fintech, payments, or adjacent regulated industries, such as card schemes, payment gateways, global acquiring, or embedded finance.

Formal training or certification in project management or agile delivery, such as PMP, PRINCE2, or Scrum Master, and comfort setting up operating rhythms including stand-ups, steering committees, and executive readouts.
Experience managing enterprise or strategic accounts as part of a broader account team, including navigating commercial sensitivities while protecting delivery quality and scope.
The ability to thrive in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment, balancing structured methodologies with pragmatic decision-making to keep complex projects moving forward.

bullets: You own the outcome and you don't wait for permission to fix what's broken.
You're comfortable with ambiguity. Give you a problem, not a prescription, and you'll run with it.
You connect dots across functions and hold the big picture without losing grip on the details.
You over-communicate by design. You'd rather flag something early than let it become a surprise.
You’re comfortable operating across time zones with a globally distributed team, including colleagues based in APAC and EMEA.

sections.title: About BJAK
paras: If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

sections.title: The Role
paras: BJAK is building a Neobank Superapp for Southeast Asia. As a Technical Product Manager, you’ll own a product vertical end to end—such as payments and expense management, remittance, insurance, or wealth and trading—from strategy, outcomes, and roadmap through to the technical design and delivery of the systems behind it.
This is a product where real money moves, mistakes are immediately visible, and licensing, compliance, and third-party rails are core product constraints—not considerations around the edges.

We are AI-native by default, but AI is a means, not the goal. The bar is knowing where a model can genuinely improve an outcome, where deterministic systems must remain in control, and how to build products that are reliable, auditable, and trusted when money is involved.

sections.title: What you'll be doing
bullets: Own a vertical end-to-end — outcomes and metrics, a backlog prioritised by value / risk / dependency / strategic priority, acceptance criteria crisp enough to build and test against.

Shape the technical design with engineering — system boundaries, money-movement correctness (idempotency, ledgering, reconciliation), third-party-rail reliance and rail-down behaviour, failure/retry/refund paths, security, latency, scalability, recovery.
Make hard trade-offs across correctness, speed, cost, reliability and UX — and defend them to an engineering, compliance or ops lead who pushes back.

Treat regulated constraints as first-class product inputs — licensing scope, CDD/KYC and limits, sanctions/PEP screening, transaction monitoring, data residency and privacy. Know which are hard launch gates and which are forward-readiness.

Apply AI where it earns its place — define what it's allowed to decide, where a human stays in the loop, how it's evaluated, and what it does when unsure. Every AI-surfaced number traces back to a real record.
Ship against external gates — build feature-complete behind flags; go live per rail as each partner and regulatory gate clears.
Work across Engineering, Design, Compliance, Operations, Treasury and Finance/Reconciliation.

sections.title: What you'll need
bullets: Product leadership — significant experience owning a complex technical product end-to-end; strong judgement and decisiveness under ambiguity; ability to balance ambition against technical, regulatory and operational reality; can hold their own with senior engineers.

Technical foundation — solid system design (boundaries, datastores, queues/workflows, APIs, failure modes, consistency under concurrency); comfort reading, reviewing and challenging design docs; can sketch an architecture and a sequence. No production code, but technical enough that engineers don't have to simplify.

Domain — experience in a regulated / high-consequence domain (payments, banking, remittance, insurance, …) or demonstrable fast-ramp ability; understands why money movement is different (correctness over convenience, irreversible states, partners you don't control).

AI judgement — hands-on with LLM-based products; can frame a feature as eval-able (offline, online, human feedback); realistic on hallucination/drift/data gaps, including data-blocked vs model-blocked and when a model must not be in the loop at all.

Nice to have — engineer or highly-technical-PM background · zero-to-one · shipped AI-heavy consumer products · defined eval metrics for ML/LLM systems · AI UX + failure-handling intuition · SEA market experience.

1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

sections.title: About This Role
paras: One million patients a month ask for a referral to a mental health provider. When they search on Headway, the order of results decides who books and who gives up. You own that order.

The scope is patient–provider matching: the retrieval and ranking systems, the strategy for where they go next, how we think about our data strategy and platform to . Your mission: maximize successful matches. Not clicks. Not bookings. Patients who connect with a provider, stay in care, and get better.

It's the most technical PM seat in the Patient org. The ranking stack is ML-powered, and the roadmap runs deep: learned relevance models and semantic and free-text search. You'll set that roadmap and get the executive team behind it, working with a dedicated pod of search and ML engineers and embedded data scientists. This is not a role for someone who needs a well-defined problem. The best candidates have a track record of finding the right problem and convincing the organization to solve it.

sections.title: Problems You'll Solve:
bullets: Understanding what patients actually need. Patients rarely arrive knowing the right filters. We're building search that lets someone describe what they need in their own words and still surface the right providers. Semantic search, LLMs, and embeddings are all in play.
Ranking for the relationship, not the click. A ranker that optimizes for conversion alone can win the booking and lose the patient. Rebuild it to optimize for care relationships that last.
Expertise. Every patient should land with a provider who has real experience helping people like them.
Marketplace health. Patients need care fast. Providers across the network need to build caseloads. When those two pull in opposite directions, you make the call.

sections.title: You Will:
bullets: Set the strategy for search, retrieval, and ranking, and get engineering, data science, design, clinical, and the executive team behind it.
Run the experimentation program end to end: hypotheses, objective functions, guardrail metrics, honest readouts. Report the losses too.
Build the data, evaluation, and ML platform foundations that unlock the next two to three years of matching work.
Work daily with ML engineers and data scientists on model objectives, features, and evaluation. You won't write the models. You will be a real thought partner on what they optimize.

Carry ranking's priorities across the company. Ranking touches patient experience, provider growth, clinical quality, and payer partnerships; resolving those competing priorities is the job, not a distraction from it.
Set the bar for technically grounded product work across the PM team.

sections.title: The Role:
paras: AML operations teams are making high-stakes decisions on bad tooling. False positive rates hitting 90–95%. SAR narratives written by hand. Alert queues backlogged for days. Investigation workflows duct-taped across a transaction monitoring system, a case management tool, and a spreadsheet no one owns.

AI has gotten good enough to fix most of this - but compliance teams don't trust it yet, and most AI vendors don't understand AML well enough to earn that trust. You will own the product that earns it.

At Oscilar, you'll have full product ownership of our AML and financial crimes suite: transaction monitoring, KYC/KYB, screening, case management, SAR filing, and the AI agents that are beginning to augment and automate the investigation workflow itself. This is not a handed-down playbook. You are writing it.

sections.title: What You'll Own:
bullets: Screening. Sanctions (OFAC, UN, EU), PEPs, adverse media, and negative news. You understand the matching problem - why fuzzy matching on names produces the false positive rates it does, and what it takes to make screening defensible to an examiner without generating alert volumes that bury the ops team.

SAR Filing & Regulatory Reporting. FinCEN SAR workflow end-to-end: narrative generation, supporting documentation, filing status, audit trail. You've seen what regulators look for in an MRA and you build product that holds up under that scrutiny.

sections.title: How You'll Work:
bullets: You are an AI-native PM. You use AI tools throughout your entire workflow — not as a novelty, but as a force multiplier that lets you do in a day what used to take a week.

For building : You use AI to generate first-draft PRDs, stress-test your own specs, write and iterate on user stories, prototype UI flows, and pressure-test edge cases before engineering touches them. Your specs are tighter and your stakeholder review cycles are shorter as a result.

For design : You use AI to explore multiple UX directions quickly and give the design team a sharper brief. You're not a designer - but you use AI tools well enough that you show up with something specific rather than a blank page.

For analysis : You use AI to query product and operational data, interpret model outputs, and build the evidence base for roadmap decisions. You don't wait for a data analyst to unblock you.
This is how we build. If you've already made AI tools a core part of your workflow, you'll find us a natural fit.

sections.title: Requirements:

You've worked in an environment where regulatory guidance was unclear, evolving, or in conflict with shipping speed - and you made the call anyway.
Bias toward speed. You use AI tools to move faster, test sooner, and learn earlier. You do in a week what takes a month elsewhere.

ashby:partly.com:4b33ce37-d58c-48c2-8d24.summary: Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. sections.title: 🚀 Our Story
paras: Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists and AI at Partly .

sections.title: 🖍️ This role
paras: In our Solutions Engineer role you'll be the technical engine behind new-market deals across the US, turning messy real-world problems into signed pilots, and putting genuinely differentiated AI in front of the people who run the repair industry.

Here's what you'd be working with. Partly runs two connected layers. Partly.com is the infrastructure platform, the B2B layer that powers parts data, cataloguing, and procurement across hundreds of integrations globally. Partly.ai is the AI tool for repairers, built on top of that infrastructure, that makes finding and sourcing the right part feel like magic. Both are powered by Interpreter, Partly's proprietary foundation model for understanding automotive parts at scale, trained on licensed OEM build data across 52+ manufacturer agreements and continuously sharpened by feedback from thousands of users across our global network. No general-purpose AI model comes close on parts accuracy, and that is what makes agentic procurement automation possible at the precision the repair industry demands.

Your job is to deploy that into markets we haven't cracked yet. Automotive data is scattered around the world in complex, inconsistent formats, and the interesting work is in unifying it into something that drives a customer's business. You'll sit between Sales, Product, and Engineering, resolving the technical blockers that stand between a prospect and a deal, building demos and experimental features that show off what the Interpreter can do, and shaping how the product gets built for and applied to each new market.

sections.title: 💻 What will you do
bullets: Unblock new-market deals end-to-end. Own the technical path from first conversation to signed pilot across the UK and Nordics: scope integrations, map end-to-end estimating and parts workflows, and together with commercial team clear whatever stands between a prospect and a yes.
Build demos and experimental features. Create market demos and portal prototypes that prove what Partly can do before committing core engineering, iterating fast on what prospects react to.
Run Technical Readiness Assessments. Produce the TRAs that map a customer's systems and dependencies, so both sides know exactly what a pilot requires.
Turn data into a commercial case. Build value-proposition frameworks, calculators, and reporting (for example, insurer reporting dashboards) that show customers the value in their own numbers.
Be the voice of the US customer to Product. Translate recurring deal blockers into clear, prioritised product asks, and shape how the product gets built and applied for each new market.

The safety net’s strength depends not just on funding, but delivery. Propel exists to dramatically improve how government benefits are delivered. Managing SNAP benefits, picking a D-SNP plan, or protecting against EBT theft should feel as seamless as Apple Pay or Netflix.

Governments struggle to build modern, scalable user experiences. We don’t.

Over 5 million Americans trust Propel today. We’ve grown revenue 35% YoY and are reinventing entire benefit categories, including Medicare, around the real needs of low-income Americans. We’re building a high-growth, high-ceiling, sustainable for-profit company where impact drives revenue.

You’ll run recurring state meetings and weekly updates, track commitments on both sides, and manage scope against the statement of work, offering a lower-lift path when a request doesn’t fit, and pushing on core platform capabilities when the investment makes sense.

Make each launch easier than the last. You’ll build the playbook for how we should go from discovery to data access to launch, and turn patterns across engagements into evidence-based recommendations for Product and Government Partnerships.

bullets: Experience running discovery directly with customers inside complex organizations and turning it into a scoped roadmap that both sides agree on.

ashby:pylon:8a1ad19d-f636-4bd5-8662-d1ed.summary:
America’s $13T mortgage market is one of the most important financial systems in the world. It underwrites the middle class and is the mechanism through which millions of families build wealth. But while every other financial instrument has been simplified to an API call, mortgages are still assembled by hand.

We started from zero and created the first vertically integrated mortgage platform that turns origination into a single API.

Publicly traded companies and the country’s largest originators are already building on Pylon. Revenue is compounding monthly. We’re backed by Peter Thiel, Conversion Capital, QED, Citi, Fifth Wall, and the founders of Ramp, Blend, and Mercury.

sections.title: About Pylon
paras: Working at Pylon isn’t for those seeking comfort. The people who thrive here have high agency, strong opinions, and a track record of delivering outcomes without direction. Many of us are former founders. We move quickly, challenge each other directly, and take full ownership of results. It’s hard work, but it will be worth it.
Join us in building America’s mortgage rails .

sections.title: About the role
paras: Every customer runs their mortgage business a bit differently. They have their own systems, teams, and ways of serving borrowers, and Pylon only works if it fits into how they actually operate.

We’re hiring a Lead Forward Deployed PM to embed with our most strategic customers, learn their business from the inside, and build Pylon into the way they work. You’ll spend time with their loan officers, operations teams, and engineers, figure out how loans really move through the organization, and map out how to put Pylon at the center of it.

This is a senior role. You’ll work directly with customer executives and technical leaders, take charge of complicated, high-stakes projects, and push them to real results, even when that means asking customers to change how they work.

sections.title: What you’ll do
bullets: Embed with strategic customers, on site and remotely, to understand their teams, systems, and full mortgage workflow
Map how each customer works today, figure out where Pylon adds the most value, and put together a plan that gets them live quickly
Own each integration from scoping and solution design through data mapping, configuration, testing, and launch, working with their engineers and ours
Find the manual steps, workarounds, and bottlenecks in each customer’s process and replace them with Pylon
Write and ship code yourself, including integrations, scripts, configurations, internal tools, and agents on our platform, and commit changes to our core codebase when a customer needs them
Bring what you learn back to the product team. You’ll figure out which requests are one-offs and which should become part of the core platform, and work with product to build them

Be the person accountable for each engagement. You’ll work directly with customer executives and technical leaders to set goals, get everyone aligned, make the hard calls, and hold both sides to the results
Advise customer leadership on how to modernize their mortgage operations, and work with GTM and Account Management to support deals, grow relationships, and make sure customers succeed

sections.title: About you
bullets: You have strong opinions and you’ll defend them, including with customers. We argue about decisions a lot here, and we’ll ask you to explain your thinking and stand behind it. We also expect you to change your mind when someone shows you you’re wrong.

You’re ruthless about priorities. Customers will ask for everything. You focus on what gets them live and what creates the most value, and you’re comfortable saying no to good ideas that come at the wrong time.

You’re comfortable in a heavily regulated market. Compliance is non-negotiable for us. We work with regulators to push the industry forward and get better outcomes for borrowers. We play by the rules, and we play to win.
You care a lot about our customers and their borrowers, and you hold a high bar for them. We’ll do whatever it takes to make them successful on Pylon.

You default to software over manual work. One of our guiding principles is that anything in the backend mortgage process done by a human is a bug, and you’ll see more of these bugs than anyone else at Pylon. When we need a temporary workaround, you flag it, write it down, and push for the real fix.

You’re good with people. You’ll work with everyone from loan officers and operations teams to engineers and executives, at our customers and inside Pylon, and you know how to build real relationships and get results through them.
You have a lot of ideas. You notice things that could be better about the product, our customers, and the team, and we’ll give you room to act on them.
You’re willing to get into the weeds. You can learn mortgage quickly enough to sound like a 20-year veteran, and you can learn each customer’s business as well as their own team knows it.

sections.title: The Role
paras: We're looking for a pulmonologist who wants to build better tools for pulmonary care. In this Senior Product Manager role, you'll use your firsthand clinical experience to own one or more care pathways in our Pulmonary suite—from understanding the problem in clinic to testing solutions with clinicians and bringing them into use.

The focus starts with COPD, AATD, and broader pulmonary clinic workflows, including asthma, within a portfolio that also includes incidental pulmonary nodules and lung cancer screening. Some of this work is live with customers; some is still being built and validated.

We welcome pulmonologists moving from clinical practice into product, as well as those already working in product management or digital health. You do not need to have held a product management title. What matters is firsthand knowledge of pulmonary care and a track record of improving clinical workflows, implementing clinical software, or leading digital health initiatives.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own one or more pulmonary care pathways end to end, translating guidelines and evidence into patient criteria, care gap logic, and workflow design.
Lead discovery and site visits with pulmonary care teams and KOLs, and turn what you learn into prioritized problems and recommendations.
Develop requirements with our product and engineering teams, set success measures, and drive cross-functional follow-through, surfacing dependencies and blockers early.
Stay with products after go-live: identify barriers to use, partner with Customer Success, Implementation, Design, and Engineering to fix them, and use feedback and usage data to guide improvements.
Lead clinical investigation and resolution of customer issues alongside our customer-facing teams, and partner with Clinical and the CMO on claims, validation, and evidence.
Prototype and test ideas with clinicians using design and AI-assisted prototyping tools.

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: MD/DO with completed specialty training in pulmonary medicine and medical licensure, active or previously held.

3+ years of clinical practice in pulmonary medicine. Outpatient pulmonary experience is strongly preferred, including longitudinal COPD and asthma management, testing, referrals, follow-up, and care-team coordination.

Product management or digital health experience, or a track record of improving clinical workflows, implementing clinical software, or leading digital health initiatives. 2+ years of relevant experience preferred.
Structured problem-solving, clear writing, and a record of driving work to completion across teams.
Working knowledge of pulmonary guidelines and how care pathways run inside health systems.
Familiarity with EHR workflows - Epic experience preferred
Curiosity about AI products and willingness to prototype and test ideas yourself.

Experience with pharma or life sciences partners in respiratory disease.

bullets: Bring newly racked CPU and GPU servers from hardware handoff through full provisioning and configuration to production readiness

Experience moving quickly in a growing company, with high standards and limited structure.

bullets: Own the Customer Zero program as a funded initiative with a real roadmap, clear outcomes, and an operating rhythm that holds across competing priorities. You set the pace, define what done looks like, and keep the work alive without needing someone to push it. You measure yourself by business value delivered, not by meetings held.

Drive adoption of Celigo's own products (agents, MCP, Ora/CLI, integrations) inside GTO's GTM, CX, and G&A systems. When you run into friction, you dig into it before being asked. Surface what's genuinely hard, prioritize it, and shepherd it into Product's roadmap in partnership with the CPO's org.

Operate in both hats simultaneously: design the underlying business processes and own the solution as a product manager. You're the person who figures out how the process should work and the person accountable for whether what ships delivers an outstanding experience.

Weigh user needs against security, privacy, and governance considerations (RBAC, permissions, service accounts), making trade-offs deliberately rather than after the fact. Build the prescriptive playbook Product and Sales need: governance patterns, reference architectures, and proof points that hold up in enterprise conversations.

Be the external face of how Celigo runs on Celigo. Present at flagship events, join key customer and prospect conversations, and package our internal use into references Sales can put in front of prospects and existing customers. Enable Product Marketing and Sales to scale the story beyond you.

You connect your work to the bigger picture. You understand why Customer Zero matters to the company, and you make decisions that serve that outcome, including the trade-offs nobody told you to make. You ask "why" before "how."

You ship the smallest version that delivers real value and iterate on real feedback. A 10-slide internal use case that lands in one deal is better than a perfect playbook no one has read. You recover quickly when something doesn't land, without drama.
You treat the program's problems as your own. You move on things before being asked, you measure yourself by outcomes rather than activity, and you find the faster path and take it.
You drive results through influence, not authority. You create alignment with engineering teams, Sales, and the CPO's org by understanding what each team needs and making it easy for them to say yes.

You're comfortable applying AI to your own work: drafting, research, analysis, and wherever else it frees you for the judgment calls that matter. Genuine curiosity about what AI can and cannot do is part of what makes someone thrive here, especially in a role that's also responsible for making AI credible to customers.
You translate clearly between business stakeholders (GTM, CX, G&A) and technical teams. You know enough about the systems to design processes, not just manage a backlog.

Strong command of the OSI model and core protocols: TCP/IP, TLS (including TLSv1.3 and mTLS), DNS, HTTP/2.
Deep understanding of Zero Trust technologies: Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA), Secure Web Gateway (SWG), Remote Browser Isolation (RBI), Data Loss Prevention (DLP), CASB, and Cloud Email Security.

Deep understanding of internet and security technologies: forward and reverse proxies with content filtering & DLP, sandboxing, firewalls/NGFW, WAF, bot management, rate limiting, and SSL/IPsec & SSL/TLS VPN appliances and services.

Modern identity: SSO via SAML and OIDC, SCIM user/group provisioning and deprovisioning, LDAP/Active Directory, MFA/FIDO2, and the role of the IdP — with hands-on experience on Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, or Ping.
DNS in depth: DNS filtering, DoH/DoT, conditional forwarding / split-DNS, internal-zone resolution, and local domain fallback.

greenhouse:faire:8872787002.summary: Faire is a technology wholesale platform built on the belief that the future is local. At Faire, we're using the power of tech, data, and machine learning to connect this thriving community of entrepreneurs across the globe. Picture your favorite boutique in town — we help them discover the best products from around the world to sell in their stores. With the right tools and insights, we believe that we can level the playing field so businesses can grow and local communities can thrive.

sections.title: About this role
paras: Faire’s Brand Partnerships team brings the most sought-after brands onto Faire. For many of these brands, the deal is won or lost on the technical sale: whether their catalog, inventory, pricing, and orders can flow cleanly between their systems and Faire, and how much work it takes to get there.

That's the work we're hiring for. Brands connect to Faire in three ways: native platform apps, a curated network of middleware and EDI partners, or a custom build on Faire's public API. Integrated brands perform better on Faire, with fuller catalogs, more accurate pricing, and fewer stockouts. We already have integration expertise, tooling, and a solution design process in place. What we don't have yet is a true solutions engineering muscle: someone who pairs deep integration knowledge with a seller's instincts and brings integration into every deal earlier.

As our Solutions Engineer, you'll be the technical counterpart to our Enterprise Account Executives across NAM and EU. You'll also partner with Brand Success Managers on existing brands. You'll own the technical win from the first discovery call through integration go-live, and you'll help turn the foundation we've built into a repeatable solutions engineering motion. As the function grows, there's real room for this role to grow with it. Expect about three quarters of your time on new enterprise deals with the AEs. The rest is the hardest escalations on live brands. Integration Support runs the day-to-day queue.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Qualify for technical feasibility early - From the first call, run technical discovery with Enterprise AEs.
Map the brand's stack: commerce platform, ERP, WMS/3PL, shipping and label tools, and any existing EDI or middleware.
Find the source of truth for catalog, inventory, and orders.
Tell AEs and leadership which deals are worth prioritizing, what's feasible, and where the risk sits.
Flag early when a brand's technical team can't match the pace of the deal.

Build the business case - Show brands why integrating beats managing Faire manually. Lay out timeline, total cost (including middleware fees against margin), and weekly operational hours saved, in terms a brand's CFO and operations lead can sign off on.

Design the solution - Recommend the right path for each brand: a native app (Shopify, WooCommerce, PrestaShop), a middleware or EDI partner, or a custom build on our API. Weigh the brand's ERP, shipping model, and IT capacity. Own the solution design so AEs can stay focused on the deal.

Close the fulfillment loop - The hardest part of most enterprise integrations is getting tracking and shipping cost back into Faire automatically, so orders close and brands get paid. Design around it from day one.

sections.title: What success looks like
bullets: First 30 days: Learn Faire's integration paths, partner network, and solution design process, and shadow live enterprise deals.
By 60 days: Lead technical discovery and solution design on active deals, and own a set of escalations end to end.
By 90 days: Extend our reference architectures to cover a common enterprise stack, and publish a technical qualification guide the AE team uses.

Ongoing:



• Enterprise activations and GMV
Time from signature to integration go-live
Brands going live with orders flowing into their systems without manual re-entry, and fulfillment data flowing back automatically

We collaborate proactively, and often. We prioritize alignment. Cross-functional partners & stakeholders engage in active working sessions, not passive status meetings. We choose to solve complex problems together rather than go back and forth in Slack.

We document for transparency. We keep stakeholders and partners informed asynchronously by centralizing progress, context and key decisions to make it easy to track project momentum and business impact.
We value data over opinion: We analyze metrics and leverage the best available information to resolve debates, ground our strategies, and make confident calls

We match rigor to the stakes. We make swift decisions with the best insights at hand, recognizing information is not always perfect. We balance our evaluation depth with the importance of the outcome and keep moving.

We build systems for scale and success. We actively architect the foundations we need to succeed. When an important process, framework, or piece of documentation doesn't exist or is broken, we build it, and we build to scale.

sections.title: About the Role
paras: Veeam is looking for a high-agency, hands-on Principal Product Manager to help define what data and AI trust looks like in the agentic era. AI is a generational discontinuity: autonomous agents now read, modify, and delete enterprise data at machine speed, and the AI factories behind them increasingly run as stateful, cloud-native workloads on Kubernetes — from AI pipelines and model artifacts to the vector databases powering RAG. The infrastructure to deploy AI exists; the infrastructure to trust it is still being built. As data resilience, data security, and AI governance converge on the Veeam DataAI Command Platform, we need a builder who can take ideas from 0 to 1 at that intersection. You’ll join a friendly, fast-moving team of builders who win together and move fast.

This is a senior individual contributor role — there are no direct reports, and your impact comes from what you build, ship, and influence, not from the size of an org chart. You’ll thrive here if you love building and are energized by ambiguity.

sections.title: What You’ll Do
bullets: Bridge data resilience, security, and AI. Connect the dots between data resilience, data security posture, and AI governance — identifying where they converge and defining products that keep customers resilient, secure, and AI-ready.

Seize the agentic AI opportunity. Shape new use cases for protecting and securing AI workloads — especially in Kubernetes environments — from detecting risky agent activity to undoing AI mistakes with precise, clean, verified recovery.

Roll up your sleeves with engineering. Work shoulder-to-shoulder with globally distributed development teams on use-case architecture and platform hardening — from authentication and logging to secrets management — and tease out the minimum viable product.

Champion security and compliance as deal accelerators. Partner cross-functionally to triage security findings into fixable work and drive compliance (e.g., SOC 2, STIG, NIST, VPAT) that unblocks regulated and public-sector deals.
Own the “why.” Articulate why we are building what we’re building, and bring engineers, customers, and leadership along once the merits are clear.

Educate customers and the field. Partner with sales and lead customers to articulate and validate the value proposition, build compelling demos and proofs of concept, and evangelize at analyst and community events.

Innovate in the eyes of the customer. Use what you learn from customers to lead the development roadmap iteratively — ship, learn, and refine in tight loops so every release reflects real-world needs.
Take initiatives from 0 → 1. Turn ambiguous ideas into validated concepts, prototypes, and first releases — creating new products and capabilities where none existed before, then scaling what works.

sections.title: What You’ll Bring
bullets: AI and agentic fluency. A working understanding of how LLMs, RAG pipelines, and AI agents are built and deployed — and the new data, identity, and recovery risks they introduce.

Cloud and infrastructure fluency. Comfortable setting up and operating your own environments across public cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP) and on-premises infrastructure, including secrets management (e.g., HashiCorp Vault).
A genuine love for building and technology. A tinkerer at heart who tests, breaks, and learns by doing.

Relevant background. Prior experience in product management and/or sales engineering; technical roles such as solutions architecture, security engineering, DevOps, or technical marketing engineering are a strong plus.
First-principles problem solving. Ability to break complex problems into simple, shippable steps and a data-centric mindset that forms convictions through rigorous analysis.
Influence without authority. Strong communication skills to engage engineers, enterprise customers, and senior leadership with clarity and credibility.

High agency in fast-moving environments. A self-starter who navigates uncharted waters, manages multiple initiatives at once, and thrives in an agile, non-hierarchical setting rather than a waterfall one.
A team-first approach. A can-do collaborator who wins as a team, builds alignment across the organization, and executes.

bullets: Own the Trading roadmap. You set milestones, surface dependencies, and keep strategic priorities honest. You make the prioritization call when everything can't ship at once.

Define and ship trading experiences. You write the specs, run user studies, iterate on feedback, partner with QA on test plans, and clear the backlog. Nothing in your charter goes live without your sign-off.

Stay close to how traders actually behave. You interview and observe customers. You ask "Show me how you currently trade and manage risk," not "Would you use this feature?" You distinguish what they say from what their behavior reveals.
Cut the hard tradeoffs. You weigh speed vs. depth, retail clarity vs. power-user needs, and compliance constraints vs. product ambition- and you own the decision.
Drive market and competitive clarity. You run the research that informs what we build next. Your work shows up in the roadmap, not a slide deck that dies in a folder.

Represent Trading across the company. You are the DRI in cross-functional forums with Engineering, Design, Analytics, Marketing, Compliance, and Growth. Alignment is your job; escalation is the exception.
Own a defined slice of the trading product line. Features in your charter are yours from inception through post-launch iteration. Ownership isn't shipping tickets- it's delivering outcomes.

Shipped software or financial products at scale. You have owned customer-facing products end-to-end and can describe a time you coordinated design, eng, and GTM through a launch- and what you did when dependencies slipped.

Data-informed, user-obsessed. You instrument your own funnel, size opportunities, and prioritize without waiting for someone to hand you the analysis- always through a compassionate lens of the trader.

Cross-functional leadership without authority. You can describe a time you aligned Design, Engineering, QA, Marketing, Compliance, and Growth toward a ship date, and how you unblocked the team when it stalled.

sections.title: About the Opportunity
paras: We're looking for a Customer Engagement Analyst to join our Customer Engagement team and become the technical and analytical backbone behind some of unitQ's largest enterprise accounts. This is the on-ramp into our Customer Engagement Manager (CEM) track — an early-career role designed for someone who wants to build a career in enterprise customer success and is willing to start by becoming exceptional at the craft: configuring the unitQ platform, running the analyses, building the artifacts, and learning how enterprise companies actually use customer signal at scale.
You will work alongside our most senior Customer Engagement Managers, supporting accounts that operate at executive altitude. The work is technical, analytical, and consequential.

You should be goal-oriented, highly organized, and a self-starter who works well independently or in a team environment. You will work closely with Customer Engagement Managers, our engineering team, and customer-side stakeholders ranging from analysts to senior leadership.

Build the artifacts that go in front of customers, including the technical and data layer of meeting decks for QBRs, executive steerings, and POC checkpoints.
Show up in customer-facing moments as the technical voice on the unitQ side — joining working sessions, training end-users, and handling first-line technical questions before they need to escalate.

In this role, you will operate as a Technical AI Product Manager, defining product vision and strategy across multiple engineering teams, translating complex validation needs into actionable roadmaps, and elevating data-driven evaluation capabilities across the organization.

We are seeking a Technical AI Product Manager with a strong systems engineering foundation to define, scale, and prioritize our AI-focused data integration and testing frameworks. You will own the product lifecycle for the evaluation and validation platforms supporting our Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) and Autonomous Driving (AD) technologies. Acting as the bridge between perception/planning engineering teams, validation leads, and global R&D stakeholders, you will drive the adoption of AI-powered diagnostics to help realize safe, reliable self-driving vehicles.

sections.title: Job Description
bullets: Architect and scale intelligent failure-triaging and automated Root Cause Analysis (RCA) frameworks capable of processing petabyte-scale simulation and real-world vehicle logs.

Apply modern AI/ML methods, including LLMs/VLMs, time-series anomaly detection, statistical pattern recognition, and causal inference, to automatically isolate failure modes across perception, planning, control, and vehicle platform layers.

Integrate automated triaging into continuous integration, regression testing, and cloud replay pipelines (SiL/HiL/ViL) to streamline software release cycles and raise validation standards across engineering groups.
Establish best practices for log data structures, automated analytics workflows, vector search and embeddings for failure-mode retrieval, and ML pipeline reliability.
Partner directly with autonomy software leads, validation engineers, and cloud infrastructure teams to align toolsets and integrate automated diagnostics into day-to-day R&D workflows.

sections.title: Qualifications
bullets: Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

5+ years of progressive experience in Technical Product Management, AI/ML Systems Engineering, or technical data analytics infrastructure within autonomous vehicles, robotics, or complex distributed systems.
2+ years of experience owning product roadmaps, defining technical requirements, and driving cross-functional alignment across multiple engineering teams.

Strong technical fluency in Python and SQL (or equivalent data languages), with deep comprehension of production-grade data pipelines, distributed execution frameworks, and testing infrastructure (hands-on coding is not required, but architectural depth is essential).
Hands-on product or technical experience managing big-data structures, robotics logging formats such as ROS/ROS2, MCAP, Protobuf, and CAN logs, and cloud data storage.

sections.title: Preferred Qualifications:
bullets: Demonstrated experience productizing applications of LLMs/VLMs, sequence modeling, pattern recognition, or vector embeddings for log classification, failure-mode retrieval, or automated root cause analysis.
In-depth understanding of autonomous driving software architectures, including perception, sensor fusion, localization, motion planning, and vehicle control.
Experience overseeing or deploying within SiL, HiL, or cloud-based replay and simulation testing setups at scale.
Working knowledge of distributed frameworks and data tools such as PySpark, Ray, Databricks/Snowflake, vector databases, Apache Airflow, Kubernetes, and AWS/GCP services.
